title: Separate reusable course assets from learner-owned state
intent: Keep course repository shareable while moving all learner progress and outcomes to an independent repository

proves: Public course and private learner repository responsibilities are explicit
does_not_prove: Existing external learner repositories were migrated

proves: Learner document templates are retained in the course repository without personal state
does_not_prove: Every future custom artifact type has a template

proves: Course deliverables are requirements/templates and personal evidence belongs elsewhere

name: New learner onboarding
nodes: write progress and artifacts only to personal repository

impact: Existing in-repository personal notes and week-01 state are no longer authoritative and must be migrated before removal
mitigation: Migrated the existing week-01 record to the designated external repository and verified it with progress-scan.v2

note: Generated weekly tutorial changes are grouped because all 32 apply the same repository-boundary wording generated from one source

title: Introduce template-driven initialization and dual-repository progress scanning
intent: Make learner setup repeatable and prevent course templates from being treated as live progress

proves: Initializer enforces separate roots, renders course templates and preserves existing learner files
does_not_prove: Remote Git repositories are created automatically

proves: Scanner CLI now requires an explicit learner repository
does_not_prove: Legacy callers have been updated outside this repository

proves: Scanner rejects identical roots and reads rules and progress from different roots
does_not_prove: Both repositories use compatible historical course versions

proves: Synthetic dual-repository states cover onboarding, separation, gates, missing files, blockers and fingerprints
does_not_prove: Hermes scheduled execution has been exercised

name: Progress detection
nodes: read learner week records and notes

compat_risk: Breaking CLI and schema change for external callers still using progress-scan.v1 or a single repository

impact: Single-repository invocations fail because --progress-repo is now required and output root fields changed
mitigation: Updated all in-repository prompts and docs to v2; external automation must update command and parser together

impact: Rolling back the course scanner would not read the external learner repository and could mistake course templates for progress
mitigation: Keep the personal repository intact; rollback requires restoring a compatible v1 state copy or retaining the v2 scanner

risk: External Hermes or other automation may still invoke the v1 single-repository command
trigger: Caller has not adopted --progress-repo or progress-scan.v2 root fields
suggested_review: Search deployed automation configuration and run one end-to-end scheduled scan before enabling unattended supervision

note: CLI, schema, consumers, documentation and deterministic tests are covered

missing: No live Hermes scheduled run was available in this workspace
impact: Prompt routing integration is validated by static review and scanner tests but not by a production scheduler
suggestion: Run one INITIAL_SCAN and one FAST wakeup with explicit course and learner repository paths

residual_risks: External progress-scan.v1 consumers require coordinated migration
